      17             I'm Senator Carl Marcellino, and I chair the

      18      Committee on Investigations and Government

      19      Operations for the New York State Senate.

      20             The purpose of this particular hearing is to

      21      consider possible infrastructure and construction

      22      improvements, zoning changes, beach protection,

      23      with rebuilding, in the aftermath of

      24      "Superstorm Sandy," to prevent the structure

      25      destruction from the next storm.





 

                                                                   5
       1             The hearing, hopefully, will begin with

       2      discussion of all the changes our state needs to

       3      make, and consider, as we rebuild after

       4      "Superstorm Sandy," and prepare for the next one,

       5      because there will be a next one.

       6             We're early in the winter, early in the

       7      season, and the next one could be tomorrow, or the

       8      next day, or the next week.  We don't know.

       9             Hopefully, we get lucky and they all bypass

      10      us, but you can't count on that, so we have to

      11      prepare, going forward.

      12             I'm joined today by my colleague

      13      Senator Jack Martins, from the neighboring Senate

      14      district to the west.  And, others of my

      15      colleagues may drop in from time to time, and/or

      16      have sent representatives to observe.  All will

      17      get copies of the report.

      18             Just by way of quick background:

      19             On October 29th of last year,

      20      "Superstorm Sandy" hit Long Island and New York City

      21      with winds over 60 miles an hour.  The storm blew

      22      down trees, power lines, and caused significant

      23      coastal flooding, resulting in 305,000 housing

      24      units destroyed and damaged.

      25             The damage from "Sandy" revealed serious





 

                                                                   6
       1      flaws in the protection, placement, and

       2      construction of our infrastructure.

       3             New York State and its municipalities need to

       4      discuss where we place infrastructure, our

       5      construction techniques, and the future evolution

       6      of our communities.

       7             Low-lying sewage treatment plants were

       8      flooded by the storm surge, resulting in hundreds

       9      of millions of gallons of raw sewage floating into

      10      New York State waters.

      11             It is estimated that the State will need to

      12      spend $1.1 billion on repairs.

      13             Appropriate planning needs to take place to

      14      prevent future damage from flooding and overflows.

      15             Coastal municipalities will consider -- since

      16      we're an island, and we're all coastal

      17      municipalities -- will consider beach-reconstruction

      18      projects, including sea wall or dune building, or

      19      nourishing beaches with additional sand.

      20             Some have suggested that these projects

      21      should have serious discussions on limiting

      22      development close to the shore; where we build, how

      23      we build.

      24             As the Governor said in the State of the

      25      State, Mother Nature has a tendency to revisit





 

                                                                   7
       1      areas she considers hers.  And when she

       2      comes, she lets us know she's there, just to

       3      give us a reminder that this is hers, and we're

       4      only tenants, and short-term tenants at that.

       5             We need to learn the lesson from "Sandy," and

       6      we need to learn the lesson from the old nursery

       7      rhyme, "The Three Little Pigs":  Mother Nature

       8      will continue to huff and puff, and we need to

       9      rebuild like the third little pig, to make sure that

      10      we survive all of the huffing and puffing of the

      11      next storm.

      12             With that, Senator Martins, if you have any

      13      opening statement?

      14             SENATOR MARTINS:  Thank you.

      15             There are lessons to be learned from the

      16      aftermath of this storm.  Certainly, we have an

      17      opportunity to learn those lessons.

      18             We paid a heavy price, as a region, to have

      19      learned those lessons.

      20             The ability now to take those and do

      21      something with it: make some changes, harden our

      22      system, prepare for the next storm.

      23             As Senator Marcellino said, there will be a

      24      next storm.  It may be tomorrow, it may be

      25      20, 30 years from now, but there will be another





 

                                                                   8
       1      storm, and we should be prepared, given what we have

       2      learned from this storm.

       3             Looking forward to the testimony today.

       4             Thank you.

       5             SENATOR MARCELLINO:  We've introduced --

       6      we've invited many speakers to come and give us

       7      solid testimony, each with certain expertise in

       8      various areas of construction, reconstruction, and

       9      so forth.

      10             Our first speaker, who I believe has done

      11      yeoman's work in leading the recovery for

      12      Nassau County, working with the county executive in

      13      Suffolk County, and nearby municipalities, like

      14      Mayor Bloomberg in the city of New York and

      15      Governor Cuomo in the state of New York, and that's

      16      our county executive, Ed Mangano, of Nassau County.

      17             Ed, you're to be congratulated on your

      18      particular efforts, your personal efforts, and the

      19      efforts of your staff, because your people work

      20      hard, and worked long hours.

      21             And I heard, in all the phone conversations

      22      that we've had, not one complaint -- "not one

      23      complaint" -- that calling Nassau County was a waste

      24      of time; that we couldn't get information; or, we

      25      couldn't get help.

       1             We never heard that coming from Nassau

       2      County.

       3             We certainly couldn't say the same for LIPA,

       4      and the utilities, but we certainly did not get

       5      complaints about how the counties; frankly, either

       6      county, handled the situation, and worked hard to

       7      protect our citizenry.

       9      thank you for what you did for our constituents and

      10      our citizens in Nassau County, and I look forward

      12             EDWARD MANGANO:  Thank you, Senator, and

      13      Chairman.

      14             And, Senator Marcellino, Senator Martins,

      15      members of the New York State Investigations and

      16      Government Operations Committee, I thank you for

      17      the opportunity to address you this morning on

      18      behalf of Nassau County's 1.3 million residents.

      19             I would also like to thank New York State,

      20      Governor Cuomo; certainly, Senators Marcellino and

      21      Martins, and our Assembly, for your partnership with

      22      response and recovery efforts following

      23      "Hurricane Sandy."  Truly worked together as a team

      24      to assist our residents.

      25             Clearly, "Superstorm Sandy" dwarfed our





 

                                                                   10
       1      region, affecting the lives of nearly every

       2      resident.  In fact, in excess of 70,000 homes and

       3      businesses were damaged, flooded, and many were

       4      completely destroyed in Nassau County.

       5             Critical infrastructure, including our power

       6      utility, wastewater treatment plants in Bay Park

       7      and Long Beach, hospitals, schools,

       8      nursing homes, police precincts, roadways,

       9      waterways, beach front, and traffic lights, all

      10      suffered destruction.

      11             Today we focus on recovery and rebuilding.

      12      Your partnership in the rebuilding process will

      13      assist Nassau County in addressing the following

      14      areas:  Home restoration, business-recovery

      15      assistance, critical infrastructure restoration, and

      16      environmental restoration.

      17             Each of the aforementioned areas of need

      18      require cooperation among county, state, federal,

      19      and local municipalities.

      20             Home-rebuilding issues in Nassau County

      21      include:

      22             Assisting non-insured and underinsured

      23      residents in the rebuilding process;

      24             Launching mold-mitigation programs to make

      25      certain that the homes are rebuilt safely, with





 

                                                                   11
       1      health in mind, and do not become sick homes in the

       2      future;

       3             And, certainly, smart rebuilding analysis,

       4      which you touched upon on your remarks, and that

       5      includes raising homes where appropriate.

       6             And we are engaged in discussion, with both

       7      state, county, and federal teams, on whether

       8      certain areas should be rebuilt at all.

       9             Now, with the advent of the funding coming

      10      through, passing Congress, and now with an

      11      optimistic eye that it will pass the Senate and

      12      signed into law, we'll have the great opportunity to

      13      work with the State, and anticipate programming to

      14      meet these needs, and build smarter, stronger, to

      15      avoid this extent of devastation should we be faced

      16      with another natural disaster, which I understand,

      17      and know, and I commend you for, is your goal of

      18      this Committee.

      20      they require assistance beyond the traditional

      21      Small Business Association loan in order to fully

      22      address small-business restoration.

      25      post "Hurricane Irene," that superstorm, many of our

       1      coastal businesses availed themselves of the

       2      Small Business Loan program.  They took on that loan

      10      work on and address, and requires additional

      11      programming.  We're engaged, obviously, in

      16      welfare.

      18      cooperative effort with the State DEC and the

      19      federal EPA, engineers and experts alike, in

      23      Park and Long Beach wastewater treatment plants

      24      protect nearly 600,000 of the 1.3 million

      25      residents here in Nassau County.  And they also





 

                                                                   13
       1      serve critical infrastructures: hospitals,

       2      schools, police precincts.

       3             So it's absolutely necessary we proceed on a

       4      path that hardens our infrastructure and

       5      protects the public from future natural

       6      disasters.

       7             And, of course, environmental restoration,

       8      beach restoration, dune restoration, and waterway

       9      cleanup programs are necessary to return our

      10      environment to pre-"Sandy" conditions and continue

      11      our restoration efforts.

      13      consideration and thoughtful partnership assisting

      14      residents in rebuilding their homes and

      15      businesses, hardening our critical infrastructure,

      16      and restoring our environment through cooperative

      17      programming.

      19      compliment the Senators here, and the leadership

      21      the State, the county, the towns, and local

      24      launch, the most thoughtful, efficient,

      25      reconstruction and rebuilding plans that are





 

                                                                   14
       1      possible.

       2             And that is an important task that we have,

       3      and it is one that I am totally encouraged that

       4      everyone is taking very seriously.

       5             We've had the wonderful opportunity, worked

       6      very closely with our partners in Suffolk County.

       7             We continue to look at Long Island as a

       8      region, and look forward to continuing to work

       9      together, and program the dollars that come

      11      our residents, protect our critical

      15      that you may have.

      25             And they deserve the greatest recognition and





 

                                                                   15
       1      respect, all of those, and the employer of the

       2      County, that stepped up to help our citizens.

       4             SENATOR MARCELLINO:  Thank you,

       5      Mr. Mangano.

      25             I certainly commend you, especially both of





 

                                                                   16
       1      your comments at the LIA breakfast recently, where

       2      you both reaffirmed that regional approach.  I think

       3      that's the way to go.

       4             We are one people on this island, and we have

      13             Thank you, Ed.

      14             SAMUEL CHU:  First, I would like to thank

      15      Senators Marcellino and Martins, and the entire

      16      Committee, for this opportunity to address this

      17      Committee, and provide you with information that

      18      will assist you in responding to the needs resulting

      20      the -- County Executive Bellone, as well as the

      22             And while they're on their way out, I want to

      23      echo the sentiment of the -- County Executive

      24      Mangano.  It really has been a good experience

      25      working with them in a difficult time.  You know,





 

                                                                   17
       1      not having to worry about going across county lines,

       2      and being able to work on a regional basis to solve

       3      problems.

       4             To address the issues that this Committee

       5      is raising today, and to provide you with insight

       6      into the situation of Suffolk County, I would like

       7      to bring to your attention the following:

       8             Our barrier beaches, including Fire Island,

       9      provide critical protection, as you all know, not

      10      just to the beaches themselves, but to tens of

      11      thousands of homes on the mainland.  They are as

      12      critical to protecting Suffolk County as the levies

      13      are to New Orleans that we heard so much about

      14      post "Hurricane Katrina."

      15             During "Sandy," and the nor'easters and

      16      storms afterward, breaches at these beaches,

      17      including at Smith's Point, Old Inlet, and Cupsogue,

      18      have led to significant mainland flooding in

      19      communities, including Lindenhurst, Amityville, and

      20      Mastic Beach.

      21             "Sandy" left, but the Atlantic Ocean

      22      continues to be a threat to these communities.

      23             And anyone who had the opportunity to

      24      experience these new inlets can tell you, it was a

      25      very -- a very astonishing thing to witness as a





 

                                                                   18
       1      south shore resident.

       2             Initial efforts by the U.S. Army Corps of

       3      Engineers, after "Sandy," to repair breaches and

       1      mentioned by County Executive Mangano, considering
